studies.label: Pairit ad-creation experiment (human-AI versus human-human teams), with human and AI evaluations and a subsequent ad campaign on X
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Individuals were randomized before matching (PDF p. 14, Section 3.3); teams were formed afterward. Participant regressions report heteroskedasticity-robust SEs without team clustering. Human and AI quality regressions cluster SEs by ad, not creator or team (PDF pp. 22, 47, 49, 51-52). Team productivity uses one observation per team and robust SEs (PDF p. 47, Table B).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 15, Section 3.4 (Participants), final analyzed sample
counts_source.quote: exclude them from all analyses, yielding a final sample of 2,234 participants (1,258 human-AI, 976 human-human).

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: A participant collaborates with an autonomous GPT-4o agent in a shared workspace. The agent chats, edits copy, selects images, and generates images through Dall-E 3; the human submits the ads. Partner identity is disclosed after the task (PDF pp. 11-12, 14-15).

arms.name: Human-Human
arms.description: A participant collaborates with another participant in the same shared workspace. Both have access to Dall-E 3 image generation; submitted ads require both participants to confirm. This is an active human-partner comparison (PDF pp. 11, 14-15).

studies.task: Create display advertisements for a think tank report by writing a headline, primary text, and description and selecting or generating an image during a timed collaborative session (PDF pp. 11, 14-16).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI gpt-4o-2024-08-06 agent on Pairit; Dall-E 3 image generation available in both arms
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 3.2, names gpt-4o-2024-08-06; PDF p. 11, Section 3.1, specifies shared Dall-E 3 access. Year refers to the dated GPT-4o model version.

preregistration.where: osf.io/jfzha and osf.io/95dhu (PDF p. 11, footnote 1); field campaigns also described as preregistered at osf.io/95dhu (PDF p. 18, Section 3.9).

open_items: The PDF does not supply unambiguous total or arm-specific counts at randomization, the assignment ratio, or attrition by arm. Its abstract describes the analyzed cohort as randomized; the detailed flow distinguishes entrants, completers, and exclusions without consistent allocation counts (PDF pp. 1, 14-16). n_randomized is null.

Participant-flow and human-human team totals conflict in the source. Completers, excluded sessions, final analyzed people, reported attrition, and Table 1 team counts do not reconcile. Retain the printed analyzed people rather than repair counts arithmetically (PDF pp. 15-16).

The text-submitting diversity sample has a printed total but no arm-specific people counts. It also has no observed arm means, participant SDs, or arm-specific uncertainty; the regression intercept is conditional on covariates and is not an observed mean (PDF pp. 21-22).

No eligible outcome has a printed participant-level SD or usable standardized effect. All arm means are unreported as descriptive means; regression intercepts have not been relabeled or combined with coefficients to obtain levels. No standardized effect or interval was calculated.

The exact number of creative-task participants contributing to the human-rating and AI-rating regressions is not printed. Rating/output observation counts must not be treated as participant counts, and people who produced no output cannot automatically be included (PDF pp. 17, 22, and 52).
Rater recruitment, survey entry, and completed-rating totals are not reconciled by the paper. No retained-rater count is derived from them (PDF p. 17, Section 3.8; PDF p. 22, Table 2).

The paper does not explain attribution of jointly confirmed ads to human-human partners. Participant models report robust rather than team-clustered SEs, and rating models cluster by ad rather than participant/team. Team productivity uses a different aggregation and has inconsistent people/team counts; appropriate precision for synthesis remains unresolved (PDF pp. 15-16, 19, 22, 47, 49, and 51-52).
Ad-copy completion has no stated numerator, denominator, or scoring/coding procedure. Its measure code is null pending that information (PDF pp. 48-49, Appendix E).

The preregistrations are named, but the PDF does not identify their preregistered primary outcome. The paper calls productivity, quality, and diversity primary in its results section; that does not establish preregistered-primary status (PDF pp. 11, 18, and 21).

The excluded field analyses have inconsistent corpus/sample counts and do not define the actual rows behind the view-metric observation count. No field row unit or creative-participant count can be inferred (PDF pp. 16, 18-20, 25, and 53).
The paper provides analysis data and code only upon request; the GitHub link is rating-survey software, not posted analysis data. No data-derived statistics were used (PDF pp. 17 and 39).
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11 from both independent extractions, the supplied diff, the screening form, the citation record, and the saved PDF. Read all 116133 characters of the markdown in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendices A-L. Extracted the cited PDF pages with pymupdf and recovered the result tables with find_tables, using cropped text-based table detection where the default detector found no table. PDF page indices plus one and printed page numbers coincide. The two differences listed by the comparison script are resolved; neither only_in_a nor only_in_b contains an estimate. All thirteen existing estimates are retained, and no additional eligible estimate was found. S1-O1 through S1-O9 are represented, including the two participant-productivity specifications, team productivity, and all three ad-copy completion outcomes. S1-O10 through S1-O13 are listed in not_extracted because their field models adjust for post-treatment ad ratings and/or campaign spend. Work-process-adjusted quality models and mechanism/moderation analyses are also listed there. The field campaign and the independent evaluators assess outputs of the same creative-task sample, not another randomized sample of creators. Agreement was independently checked for study and arm counts and for every estimate’s counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person. The full analyzed cohort is the printed people count; diversity has its own text-submitting participant sample. Ratings, ads, and teams remain observation counts rather than people. Missing creator counts and diversity arm counts remain null. Output diversity is across_people and higher_is more_diverse; productivity is with_ai/fluency and higher_is more_ideas; text and image quality are with_ai/usefulness and higher_is more_creative; click likelihood and completion are with_ai/other with their directions explained. All outputs were created during the assisted session, and assignment was between people: outcome_with_ai is true and within_person is null throughout. Later evaluation of the same outputs is not after_ai. The comparison is ai_vs_active: a GPT-4o teammate versus a human teammate, with Dall-E 3 access shared across arms; the Human-Human arm’s other_aid label refers to the randomized human-partner aid, not absence of generative image tools. Participants were randomized before matching, so teams are not coded as randomized clusters. Participant models use robust SEs without reported team clustering, human ratings use ad clusters, and AI ratings use ad clusters on output observations. The team model retains se_basis unclear because the permitted vocabulary does not identify a team-level basis for this individually randomized design; its unit itself is established as team. Demographic and personality covariates were obtained before the collaborative task; models controlling for work-process variables or later ad ratings/spend are excluded under rule 5. Distinct full-sample specifications are retained, while exact repeats between Table 2 and Tables B/G are represented once. The printed productivity percentage is recorded once with the unadjusted result, as a narrative relative effect with no calculated formula or uncertainty. No statistics were derived: unreported p-values, arm means, SDs, intervals, and standardizers remain null. Adjusted intercepts are not arm means; unadjusted intercepts labeled only as such were not relabeled as observed means. Source quotes preserve printed numeric precision and signs; standard JSON serialization can omit trailing zeros. No source-verified sample overlap is identified in the screening form. Only extraction/c392.json was written.

fixes.quote: Text, Image, Click are human ratings (7-point scale) with standard errors clustered at the ad level.
fixes.basis: The PDF explicitly clusters standard errors by ad, allowing dependence among ratings of the same output while treating ads as independent. Under the extraction-spec field notes and codebook Section 10, this is output-level uncertainty. The observation unit remains rating and n_units remains the printed number of rating observations. Ad clustering does not account for multiple ads from the same randomized creator or producing team, so it does not establish participant-level precision.
